title: Secure Peer Transport, Protocol Validation & Capability Handshake
selected_by_owner: Strict successor after owner-approved PCV-03 decomposition and PCV-03B completed_verified closeout.
objective: The direct/manual WebRTC path is a bounded, versioned, peer-bound zero-service transport with secure secret handling and a real client-measured capability handshake.
acceptance: Direct/manual WebRTC with no external ICE service is the first-class zero-service path; STUN/relay assistance remains optional and replaceable.
Every wire envelope has an explicit supported protocol/schema version and strict runtime validation; unknown/unsupported input fails safely.
Apply bounded message size, nesting, collection, batch and queued-work/backpressure limits.
Use approved secure storage for bearer/resume secret material; ordinary documents contain only safe references/digests.
Cryptographic secret generation fails closed when secure randomness is unavailable.
The joining client reports locally measured exact pack/rules/runtime/entitlement capability state rather than echoing host offer values.
Pre-auth signaling reveals only the minimum rendezvous material required for authorization.
PCV-03D+ and PCV-04 remain unauthorized until this item closes.
boundaries: Preserve PCV-03A canonical A3 identity/invitation and A5 Campaign membership authority and PCV-03B canonical A5 Session lifecycle/authority-epoch state; peer transport consumes them rather than replacing them.
Implement only the bounded, versioned, peer-bound direct/manual transport and capability-handshake surfaces authorized by PCV-03C.
Bearer/resume secret material must follow the approved secure-storage/no-plaintext boundary; ordinary product documents may contain only safe references or digests.
Do not add a generic gameplay command escape hatch; gameplay/action/combat authority remains outside PCV-03C.
Do not implement PCV-03D ordered delivery/recovery, PCV-03E presence UX, PCV-03F installed packaging/certification, or PCV-04 gameplay.
Keep direct/manual zero-service operation first-class; optional STUN/relay assistance remains replaceable and non-authoritative.
Use milestone-level OPS3 state only; no activity-journal instrumentation.
